evidence.explanation: The body enumerates fifteen problems: inadequate land/land tenure; inadequate basic/social amenities; poor farmer finances; high-interest loans/credit; farmer illiteracy; transport; storage/processing; marketing; pests/diseases; poor agricultural inputs; unfavourable climate; crude tools; inadequate extension workers; inconsistent government policies; and natural hazards/environmental degradation.

Each listed problem has at least one proposed solution; the high-interest-credit problem at 210-212 explicitly refers back to the poor-financial-status solutions at 205-208. One storage/processing solution sentence at block 235 is malformed and cannot be safely reconstructed from its wording; this is separately recorded.

open_items.detail: Week 9's assessment contains items that no 1st Term block teaches and one misdirected reading. (1) WK 9B Q2 (block 854) asks for 'compost'; 'compost' occurs nowhere else in the document and no block teaches manure making. (2) WK 9B Q4 (block 857) asks how to prevent excessive evaporation; 'mulch' occurs only at block 414 (a Week 4 pest-control question) and block 857, never in teaching text. (3) The WK 9B reading assignment (block 851) directs the learner to 'Pasture and forage crops ... pages 179-182', which is not this week's topic; the WK 9A reading (block 789) correctly cites the environmental-factors chapter, pages 212-216. (4) Block 731 lists pressure among the climate factors, but no block in Week 9 or elsewhere teaches it. (5) WK 9B Q1 (block 853) repeats WK 9A Q5 (blocks 795-796) almost verbatim. (6) Retained wording defects: block 723 runs 'CROPAND' together; block 750 has 'coaster' for coastal; block 779 has 'forms the re-growth of disease pathogen'; block 796 prints 'Soil pHB. Soil texture'; block 853 prints 'C. soil organic'; block 855 prints 'PulpB. timber'; block 801 prints 'Selective exploration', which is not the standard term (selective exploitation). No source byte is corrected here.
open_items.required_action: Record one expert decision per numbered item in AG-FACT-T1-W09-SCOPE: whether each untaught assessment item is re-scoped, replaced or removed, whether pressure is taught, and which wording is retained. Do not correct the source bytes or infer an answer key.

open_items.detail: Week 1 wording that needs an expert check before the text is delivered as teaching: (1) block 58 gives the Latin root as ‘Culture’ while block 127 uses ‘Cultura’ (the Latin noun is cultura); (2) block 107 says agriculture leads to game reserves and provides horses for horse racing and polo, which is a loose claim; (3) block 103 defines agro-based industries as those depending on agriculture for raw materials while block 105 uses ‘agro-allied industries’ for suppliers of fertilizers, pesticides, tools and machines, and Week 6 block 482 treats agro-allied and agro-based as the same; (4) block 131-132 gives pathology as the study of diseases of crops and animals while block 77 lists crop pathology as an aspect of crop production; (5) reading pages at blocks 124-125 (Iwena pages 2-6, Okafor pages 1-4) were not checked against the books. Items (1) to (4) are source wording and are retained uncorrected; no delivery correction is authored here.
open_items.required_action: Expert confirms or corrects each of items (1) to (4) with a recorded reference and says whether a delivery replacement is wanted; item (5) is checked against the listed books. Do not invent a reference.

open_items.detail: Weekend assignment Q4 at block 178 asks which item is not a source of foreign-exchange earnings in Nigeria (options include cotton, yam, cocoa and palm produce). Week 1 block 104 lists cocoa, coffee, groundnut, cotton, palm produce and timber as exports, but omission of yam from that list does not prove that yam is not exported or establish the intended answer.
open_items.required_action: Research authoritative Nigerian agricultural-export evidence and determine whether the item has a defensible answer for the source's context; if not, record a source-backed correction or mark the question unresolved. Do not infer the answer from omission alone.
